title: Again
style: cinematic horror film still, old car ferry crossing a black harbor at night, thick drifting sea fog, sodium deck lights, wet steel, rope and rust, cold teal and amber tones, dramatic moody lighting, film grain, 35mm, highly detailed, subject clearly visible, no text, no watermark
caption:
Part 2. Every night, the last ferry arrives with one extra passenger. Never the same face. 🌫️

Original fiction. Part 3 tomorrow night.

#scarystories #horrorstory #creepy #storytime #fyp

scenes.narration: Last time: twenty-three passengers boarded Owen's ferry, and twenty-four got off.
scenes.image: wet footprints on a ferry ramp leading into fog

scenes.narration: Owen tells himself he miscounted. Fog. Long shift. He writes twenty-three in the log and goes home.
scenes.image: deckhand writing in a battered logbook by lamplight in a small ferry wheelhouse

scenes.narration: The next night, nineteen board. Twenty get off. The extra is an old man in a soaked tweed cap, nodding thank you.
scenes.image: old man in a dripping tweed cap and overcoat nodding politely on a fog-bound ferry ramp

scenes.narration: The night after, a young man in a navy pea coat, water running from his sleeves.
scenes.image: young man in a vintage navy pea coat stepping off a ferry ramp, water streaming from his cuffs

scenes.narration: Every night, one extra. Never the same face twice. Always wet. Always grateful. Always gone before Owen can call out.
scenes.image: line of puddled footprints leading up a foggy dock and stopping abruptly

scenes.narration: He walks the deck during crossings. The benches. The cabin. The engine stairs. Nobody hiding. Nobody new. Until the ramp.
scenes.image: deckhand with a flashlight checking under benches in an empty ferry passenger cabin at night

scenes.narration: Captain Marta has run this route for thirty years. Owen finally asks her. She doesn't take her eyes off the fog.
scenes.image: grey-haired female ferry captain at the wheel, face lit by dim instruments, staring into fog

scenes.narration: Do you write the extras in the log? No. Good. Never write them in. If you write them in, they count.
scenes.image: close-up of the captain's weathered hands on an old ship's wheel, fog against the window

scenes.narration: Count for what? She doesn't answer. She just turns the wheel, gently, like she's steering around something in the water.
scenes.image: ferry bow pushing through black water and fog, a vague pale shape under the surface just off the side

scenes.narration: That night, the extra is the woman in the wool coat. The same woman. And this time she whispers as she passes. Thank you. Almost everyone's home.
scenes.image: close-up of a pale woman in a wet wool coat leaning close to a deckhand's ear on a foggy ramp
